record.title: Persist workspace paths with forward slashes and platform tag
record.description: Operator directive (PLAN-PATHNORM-001, decision D1 2026-10-07: delivered in P1). Persisted workspace paths, storage keys and identity hashes use '/' as the separator for all platforms; the windows: (case-insensitive) / case-sensitive: tag is kept; Windows-origin paths are detected by drive letter (C:/) or UNC (//server/share), not by separator; the UNC leading '//' is preserved; paths are converted to '\' only at OS boundaries that require it (\\?\ long-path prefixes, cmd.exe arguments, native APIs). AC1: C:\Users\example, C:/Users/example and c:/users/EXAMPLE produce one storage key. AC2: \\srv\share\x and //srv/share/x produce one storage key that still starts with //. AC3: Existing stores are converted by the --workspace-path-rekey maintenance command (decisions D5-D7 2026-10-07): after it runs no Windows-shaped workspace value contains a backslash, per-table and per-workspace row counts are unchanged, and foreign keys validate; the server refuses to start against an unconverted store (no dual-key lookup). AC4: Native file operations on Windows receive backslash paths where the OS requires them.

record.title: Test TEST-MCP-PATHNORM-001
record.notes: P1.5 2026-10-16: WorkspacePathRekeyTests cover literal Policy A normalization, collision preflight, no-backup/failed-backup refusal, read-only dry-run on explicit separate copies, transaction rollback and FK graph validation, repeat no-op, derived triage/handoff/federation identities, unchanged manual triage hashes, and startup guard. Command parser rejects missing/same copy database. Reports contain only keys/counts and retained-manual-key notice. Disposable fixtures only; no live apply.
record.description: Per BDP v4 (MockData fixture green before production code, then Real fixture). Storage-key equivalence: C:\Users\example, C:/Users/example, c:/users/EXAMPLE -> one key windows:C:/USERS/EXAMPLE; \\srv\share\x and //srv/share/x -> one key keeping leading //; \\?\C:\x -> C:/x. Remote-path detection treats //srv/share as remote. ToNativePath returns backslash paths on Windows. Rekey: value mapping f(x) touches only Windows-shaped values and is idempotent; planner builds the mapping and statement plan from a scripted snapshot; executors per provider (SQLite in-memory; SQL Server and PostgreSQL provider fixtures) rewrite all workspace columns and recompute hashed values with FK validation; report counts unchanged per table and per workspace; startup guard rejects an unconverted store; rehearsal on a restored copy of the Windows lab host's store recorded as receipts. GlobalWorkspaceId for (EXAMPLE-HOST, C:/Repos/Example) is stable across both input separators.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The native-boundary (ToNativePath) behavior for a non-Windows host is proven against a simulated host, on Windows as well, without a host-conditional skip; the Windows-host cases keep running on a Windows host.

record.title: Hostile review execution capture
record.description:
ReviewExecution entity stores model string, effort, agent, plugin/source, template id/version, run id, start/end UTC. Token counts are optional and must not be invented.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003; TEST: TEST-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003

acceptanceCriteria.text: Invalid HostileReviewWorker options fail host startup with an error that names HostileReviewWorker, on Linux and on Windows: RenewalInterval not less than LeaseDuration; MaximumActiveQueue, MaximumConcurrentReviews or MaximumAttempts below 1. AgentName, RequiredModel and RequiredEffort are not startup rules: none is pinned, and an unset one means the default (operator rule 2026-10-15; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B9). The test host owns its logging providers, so an account that cannot write the Windows Application event log cannot turn the startup failure into a logging error (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B4, triage-report-f4d47e1f, measured on the Windows lab host 2026-10-15; HostileReviewStartupAssertion_AcceptsWorkerFailureAndRejectsMaskedOrMissing, HostileReviewWorker_InvalidOptions_FailStartup, HostileReviewWorkerOptions_AnyAgentModelEffort_PassValidation).

A reviewer output is accepted with the model and effort it reports, and the execution records them, when HostileReviewWorker RequiredModel and RequiredEffort are not configured; a configured RequiredModel or RequiredEffort is required of the output, and an output reporting a different value fails the request as ModelUnavailable (operator rule 2026-10-15; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B9; tests: WorkerOptionsAndOutputRules_AcceptUnpinnedOrConfiguredAndRejectPinsOrIgnoredConfig, AcceptReviewerOutput_NoConfiguredModel_RecordsReportedModel, AcceptReviewerOutput_ConfiguredModelMismatch_FailsModelUnavailable). An output that omits the reviewer agent, model or effort records them empty (not reported), never a default model (operator decision 2026-10-15 "Empty defaults, in B9"; test: AcceptReviewerOutput_NoConfiguredModel_RecordsReportedModel).

record.title: InstallOllama provisions Ollama on Windows and Linux
record.notes: Nuke behavior is accountable through TR only (operator ruling 2026-10-10); evidence is Build.Tests, run directly as infrastructure, and the live run of the target. Created 2026-10-15 (operator decision "Approve all three (Recommended)"; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13, triage-report-680916ed).
record.description: The Nuke InstallOllama target provisions the local Ollama service the QuadBrain Ollama integration tests use (FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002), on Windows and on Linux, idempotently: when a server already answers on localhost:11434 with the required model it changes nothing; otherwise it uses an installed ollama executable (on PATH, or on Windows in Ollama's install folder LocalAppData/Programs/Ollama) or a previous portable install under the test-tools folder, else downloads that operating system's portable release into the test-tools folder (Windows: the windows-amd64 zip; Linux: the linux-amd64 archive), starts the server detached and waits until it answers, and pulls the required model (default gemma4:e4b; QBRAINAI_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL or MCP_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL overrides) when it is absent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The target's plan is chosen per operating system: a server that already answers with the required model needs no step; otherwise an installed ollama (on PATH, or on Windows LocalAppData/Programs/Ollama/ollama.exe), else a previous portable install under the test-tools folder (ollama.exe on Windows, bin/ollama on Linux), else a download of that operating system's portable release; the plan then starts the server when it is not answering and pulls the model when it is absent (Build.Tests: OllamaInstallPlanAssertion_AcceptsPerOsPlanAndRejectsWindowsOnlyOrMissingStep, then InstallOllama_Plan_PerOperatingSystem_UsesTheShippedPlanner). The required model is QBRAINAI_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL when it holds a non-blank value, else MCP_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL when it does, else gemma4:e4b, chosen by one rule that InstallOllama and QuadBrainOllamaEndpointIntegrationTests both use, proved by a unit contract over explicit inputs (operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R9-F5).
Re-running the target when the server already answers with the required model changes nothing (Build.Tests: InstallOllama_Plan_ServerAnswersWithModel_ChangesNothing over the shipped planner).

On the Linux lab host the target leaves a portable Ollama that OllamaServerFixture's resolver finds (TR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002) and the required model installed, and QuadBrainOllamaEndpointIntegrationTests run (TEST-MCP-QBOLLAMA-001).

record.title: QuadBrain Ollama endpoint integration tests
record.notes: Recorded 2026-10-15: the four tests and OllamaServerController cite this id, which the store never held (operator decision "Approve all three (Recommended)"; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13, triage-report-680916ed).
record.description: QuadBrainOllamaEndpointIntegrationTests exercise the OpenAI-compatible QuadBrain endpoint against a real local Ollama server that OllamaServerFixture adopts or starts (FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002), proving FR-MCP-QBOPENAI-001 runs the normal Creativity, Logic and Arbiter workflow without faking the LLM calls, on Windows and on Linux once InstallOllama has provisioned Ollama (TR-MCP-NUKE-016).

acceptanceCriteria.text: ChatCompletions_LocalOllamaDefaultModel_TriggersNormalBrainSlots (prompts "Hello" and "Create Hello World in C++"): with the local Ollama default model assigned to all four slots, each prompt triggers the normal Creativity, Logic and Arbiter workflow through POST /v1/chat/completions and returns non-empty content; every brain call uses that model at the Ollama endpoint, and the session log captures the brain outputs on the turn.

QBAgentRunLoop_LocalOllamaDefaultModel_DisplaysQuadBrainResponse (prompt "Hello"): QBAgent displays the QuadBrain response it received, never a placeholder; its transcript names the model QuadBrain and the QBrainAi endpoint and never the Ollama model id or endpoint.
ChatCompletions_OpenAiCompatibleFieldVariants_AreLoggedToSessionTurn: content, reasoning and reasoning_content outputs are persisted to the turn's processing dialog.

The class runs against a real local Ollama: OllamaServerFixture adopts a server already answering or starts one from a discovered executable and stops only what it started (FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002); on the Linux lab host the executable is the one InstallOllama provisions (TR-MCP-NUKE-016; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13, triage-report-680916ed).
